payload.instruction: Make this look like a comic book photo
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image visibly have comic-book styling?
node.criteria: Pass if comic-book visual styling is visibly present; fail if there is no visible comic-book styling; unknown if the image evidence is insufficient to determine this.
node.binding: Assess the overall visual treatment of the supplied image as edited, without requiring a particular technique.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image remains a realistic street photograph, with no clearly visible comic-book styling such as illustrated outlines, halftone shading, or stylized colors.

fulfillment: The node’s criteria correctly distinguish comic-book styling from retained photographic content, and the traces are valid, queried, and high-confidence; this is not a transport or dependency failure. The edited image appears largely photographic, with at most subtle contrast/texture changes and no clearly legible comic-book treatment, so the styling failure is supported. The mismatch is in aggregation: the rubric says “no” when no requested change has progressed, but the node counts unchanged photographic subject matter as progress and therefore returns “partial.” Clarify that s2 passing counts only if the edit newly establishes or materially preserves the requested photographic appearance as part of the requested combination—not merely because the source already contained a photograph. Keep the comic-book styling check independent and evidence-based, and compare source with edit where needed to distinguish actual progress from inherited content. Do not force “no” from the reference label alone; retain partial if there is genuine progress on a requested component.
s2: The node is valid and high-confidence, so this is not a transport or dependency issue. Its current question only tests whether photographic content remains; that can pass on the unchanged source and be miscounted as progress toward “Make this look like a comic book photo.” Keep the photographic-retention criterion, but make its binding explicitly distinguish retained photographic subject matter from evidence that the requested comic-book treatment was applied. Compare source and edit when judging change, and do not let inherited photographic appearance alone establish progress. Keep the styling assessment independent and evidence-based: the edit appears to retain the street photograph with little clearly legible comic-book treatment, but do not infer absence solely from low confidence or variation. Preserve unknown when the images do not support a reliable comparison, and do not use the reference label as atomic ground truth.
